title: Three former North Dakota athletes to compete at NCAA Division I track championships
text:
Three former North Dakota athletes to compete at NCAA Division I track championships
Three former North Dakota High School Activities Association track and field athletes will compete at the 2026 NCAA Division I National Track & Field Meet in Eugene, Oregon this week, according to a June 10 announcement.
The championships will take place from Wednesday, June 10 through Saturday, June 13. Both men's and women's events are scheduled simultaneously. The athletes representing North Dakota high schools include Paul Olson of North Dakota State University, Anthonett Nabwe of the University of Minnesota, and Kelsie Belquist of the University of Nebraska.
Olson, a junior at North Dakota State University and a 2022 Kindred High School graduate, is set to participate in the men’s decathlon on June 10-11. The event begins at 3 p.m. Central Time on Wednesday. Olson enters ranked 24th among NCAA qualifiers based on season-best marks. During his high school career with Kindred High School, Olson won state titles in the Class B boys high jump and 400 meter dash as a senior in his first year competing in track and field. He also placed second in the 200 meters and third in the 100 meter dash that year.
Anthonett Nabwe, a redshirt junior at Minnesota and member of the U.S. Track & Field and Cross Country Coaches Association Bowerman Award watch list, will compete in both women’s hammer throw and shot put events at nationals. Nabwe was a five-time individual state champion for Jamestown High School across shot put, discus, and javelin (as a senior), with additional podium finishes in sprints during her prep years.
Kelsie Belquist is competing as a sophomore for Nebraska in both women’s 400-meter hurdles—where she broke her university's long-standing record with a time of 55.24—and as part of Nebraska’s women’s 4x400 meter relay team. Belquist won ten individual NDHSAA Class B girls state championships during her prep career for New Rockford-Sheyenne High School and was named North Dakota Gatorade Girls Track & Field Athlete of the Year for 2023.
Further information about the NCAA Division I Track & Field National Championships can be found by following NDHSAA on social media or visiting their website.
